W1.quote: every friday i have to send my manager (priya.n@kestrel-labs.io) a quick rundown
W1.why: A schedule can only be confirmed over time, not in one practice run.

W1.quote: send my manager (priya.n@kestrel-labs.io) a quick rundown

W1.quote: a quick rundown of what the design team actually finished that week
W1.summary: The rundown covers only work the design team actually finished that week.
The source of the rundown content is the team's tracker.
The rundown should be simple and plain, without elaborate formatting or extras.
W1.why: Plainness is a matter of judgment, not a clear pass/fail check.

W2.quote: can u set up the weekly status thing for the Mobile squad??
W2.summary: The automation covers the Mobile squad's status.

W2.quote: set up the weekly status thing
W2.summary: The status report is set up to run weekly.
W2.why: A schedule's frequency can only be confirmed by its configuration, not by one practice run.

W2.summary: The report must list what is done.

W2.quote: AND whats still open + whats blocked
W2.summary: The report must also list what is still open and what is blocked.

W2.quote: so the boss can see where were stuck
W2.summary: Blocked items must be clearly visible so the boss can see where the team is stuck.
W2.why: Whether the blockers are clear enough for the boss to spot where the team is stuck is a judgement about clarity, not a fixed check.

W2.quote: send it to me i guess, tom@ortega-apps.co

W3.quote: Send it to our CTO, maya@brightfold.com

I1.quote: can you chase everyone who still owes us money?
I1.summary: Send a payment reminder to every customer who still owes money.
Customers whose invoices are already paid are left out.

I1.quote: its all in the invoices sheet
I1.summary: The invoices sheet is the source for who owes money and how much.
The first reminder to each customer is friendly in tone.
I1.why: Tone is subjective and cannot be verified by a practice run.

I1.quote: get firmer if they keep ignoring us
I1.summary: Follow-up reminders become firmer in tone when a customer does not pay after earlier messages.

I1.quote: sign it as Hannah @ Little Fern Bakery
I1.summary: Every message is signed as Hannah @ Little Fern Bakery.

I1.quote: a couple of customers are arguing about their bills rn
I1.summary: Some customers are disputing their bills, so their messages should be handled with care; the exact handling is not specified.
I1.why: The request gives no concrete rule for disputed customers, so a run cannot show a specific behavior.

I2.quote: I want ONE polite reminder once an invoice is 10 days overdue
I2.summary: Send exactly one reminder per invoice, and only once the invoice is 10 days overdue.
No further reminders are sent for an invoice after the single reminder.
The reminder message must be polite in tone.
I2.why: Politeness is a tone judgment that one run cannot verify objectively.

I2.summary: The reminder must contain no threats.

I2.quote: email me a list of who got reminded - accounts@verdant-studio.com
I2.summary: Email a list of everyone who was reminded to accounts@verdant-studio.com.
The reminder emails must be signed off as Verdant Studio.
Invoices are due 30 days after issue, so overdue status is measured from the net-30 due date.

I3.quote: set up the overdue invoice reminders
I3.summary: The automation sends reminders for overdue invoices.
Reminders go out when an invoice is 7, 21, and 45 days overdue.
A summary of the reminders is sent in addition to the reminders.
The summary is sent to ops@quill-and-ink.com.

L1.quote: anything from europe (EMEA) goes to dana@peakline.io
L1.summary: Website form leads from Europe (EMEA) are sent to dana@peakline.io.
Website form leads from the US or Canada (NA) are sent to marcus@peakline.io.
All other website form leads that are neither EMEA nor NA are sent to jo@peakline.io.

L1.quote: new leads from the website form need to go to the right person
L1.summary: Only new leads from the website form are routed, each to the correct person.

L1.quote: dont email the leads themselves, our reps do that
L1.summary: Never send email to the leads themselves; only the internal routing recipients get emails.

L2.quote: Big companies (500+ employees) go straight to our enterprise guy Raj, raj@tallyhq.com.
L2.summary: Inbound leads from companies with 500+ employees are routed directly to Raj at raj@tallyhq.com.
Inbound referral leads are routed to Sofia at sofia@tallyhq.com.

L2.quote: everything else to the shared inbox sales@tallyhq.com
L2.summary: All other inbound leads that are neither 500+ employee companies nor referrals go to the shared inbox sales@tallyhq.com.

L2.quote: Big companies (500+ employees) go straight to our enterprise guy Raj
L2.summary: Big-company leads go straight to Raj, without being sent to Sofia or the shared inbox first.

L3.quote: leads should go to whoever covers that country.
L3.summary: Each lead is routed to the person who covers the lead's country.
Leads from Germany or Austria go to Lena.
Leads from France go to Paul.
Leads from any other country go to the user.
The user's address, used for leads with no matching country, is kai@brook-tools.de.

S1.quote: if a ticket asks about shipping just reply that orders ship in 2-3 business days and they get a tracking link by email
S1.summary: Shipping-related tickets get a reply saying orders ship in 2-3 business days and the customer gets a tracking link by email.

S1.quote: just reply that orders ship in 2-3 business days
S1.summary: The shipping reply should only say orders ship in 2-3 business days (nothing else is added).

S1.quote: password questions -> tell them to use 'forgot password' on the login page
S1.summary: Password-related tickets get a reply telling the customer to use the 'forgot password' option on the login page.
All tickets that are not shipping or password questions are sent to help@cobaltcandle.com.

S2.quote: can you auto answer the easy support tickets?
S2.summary: Automatically answer the easy support tickets.

S2.quote: opening hours question -> we're open mon-sat 9-6.
S2.summary: When the ticket is an opening hours question, reply that the business is open Mon-Sat 9-6.

S2.quote: returns -> you can return anything within 30 days, just reply with your order number.
S2.summary: When the ticket is about returns, reply that anything can be returned within 30 days and ask the customer to reply with their order number.

S2.quote: the rest goes to my support lead
S2.summary: Any ticket that is not an opening hours or returns question is escalated to the support lead.
The support lead to escalate to is Gwen, at gwen@harbor-goods.com.

S3.summary: The automation should be set up as an auto-reply for support tickets.

S3.quote: If someone asks for a copy of their invoice tell them its in their account under Billing > Invoices.
S3.summary: When someone asks for a copy of their invoice, the reply tells them it is in their account under Billing > Invoices.
The invoice auto-reply is the only automated reply; no other automated replies are set up for now.
Every other ticket that is not an invoice copy request is routed to support@nimbusdesk.app.
Every auto-reply is signed with "Nimbus Support".

E1.summary: Small expenses are approved automatically without the user reviewing them.

E1.quote: send the rest to me: finance@lumen-dental.com
E1.summary: Expenses that are not auto-approved are sent to finance@lumen-dental.com.

E2.quote: anything under 200 with a receipt can be approved automatically
E2.summary: Expenses under 200 with a receipt are approved automatically.

E2.quote: anything bigger goes to my cofounder ines@parcelpoint.eu for sign off
E2.summary: Expenses of 200 or more are sent to ines@parcelpoint.eu for sign-off.

E2.quote: let people know when theirs got approved
E2.summary: The submitter is notified when their expense gets approved.

E3.quote: up to 75 bucks is ok automatically

E3.quote: doesnt matter if they forgot the receipt for small stuff

O3.summary: The automation sends a digest once per day.
